case_name: Kumari M Mythri vs Sri R Muniraju

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kumari M Mythri, minor represented by her mother and guardian Smt. A'Nalini Devi

facts_of_case: Petitioner is a minor seeking permission to alienate property in favour of intended purchaser.

legal_principles.principle: A guardian of a Hindu minor has the power to do that which are necessary for the benefit of the ward.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the natural guardian has the power to do that which are necessary for the benefit of the ward.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — Section 8

legal_principles.principle: Any disposal of immovable property by the natural guardian, in contravention of the Act, is voidable at the instance of the minor or any person claiming under him.
legal_principles.held: It is held that any disposal of immovable property by the natural guardian, in contravention of the Act, is voidable at the instance of the minor or any person claiming under him.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — Section 3

legal_principles.principle: No court shall grant permission to a guardian to do any of the acts mentioned in Section 8, except in cases of necessity or for evident advantage of the minor.
legal_principles.held: It is held that no court shall grant permission to a guardian to do any of the acts mentioned in Section 8, except in cases of necessity or for evident advantage of the minor.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — Section 8

outcome.final_order: Permission granted to the father and natural guardian of the petitioner to alienate the property in favour of the intending purchaser.
